problems.field: studies[S1].design_class (also the reconciliation.agreed_fields_checked entry for design_class, marked confirmed: true)
problems.source_says: The codebook (section 4) defines lab_rct as a randomized experiment with people in a supervised session. The session was supervised, but the paper never says that anything was randomized. All 60 participants did all four AI conditions. The order came from a 4 x 4 balanced Latin square, which is a counterbalancing scheme, and the paper does not say how participants were allocated to its sequences. The between-subjects groups were formed from a pre-test questionnaire. The only 'random' in the PDF text and in Figs. 1 and 3 is the Midjourney seed setting. The form's own assignment.randomized = not_stated and criterion 1 = unclear contradict a randomized design code. Keep a randomized code only if the authors confirm random allocation to sequences. Until then no form-spec code fits cleanly: quasi_people needs a without-AI condition, so 'other' with a note is the closest value.
problems.quote: To control for order effects, task sequences were assigned using a 4 × 4 balanced Latin square design.
problems.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.3 (Latin square); p. 6, Sect. 3.2.3 ('seed values were random'); p. 5, Sect. 3.1 (questionnaire-based groups); codebook section 4; form-spec design_class note

confirmed.statement: (a) The document never states random assignment of people or a random order of conditions. A search of the PDF text layer (all 19 pages) finds 'random' only in 'seed values were random', a Midjourney setting. Fig. 1 (procedure) and Fig. 3 (outputs by participant) are images, and neither mentions randomization. So assignment.randomized = not_stated is right, and the form's assignment quote is verbatim with correct locators.

(e) The AI conditions vary only within person: 'Each participant completed all four combinations of the 2 × 2 within-subjects conditions.' The order was counterbalanced with a 4 x 4 balanced Latin square. The paper does not say whether participants were randomly allocated to the four sequences. The codebook admits a within-person design only when the order is randomized, so criterion 1 = unclear and the form's open question to the authors are the right reading.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Sect. 3.2.2; p. 7, Sect. 3.3; codebook section 3, criterion 1

confirmed.statement: The between-subjects factors were measured, not manipulated. The pre-test questionnaire 'served as the basis for the group assignment', and participants 'were classified into two proficiency levels' and 'categorised into three experience levels'. Fig. 1 calls this step 'Preliminary testing and grouping', with 'A 3×2 group design, with 10 people per group'. Neither factor is an AI condition. Unit within_person_order and structure mixed match the paper's 'mixed-factorial design'.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Sects. 3 and 3.1; p. 6, Sect. 3.2.2 and Fig. 1

confirmed.statement: (b) Each condition gave participants a generative image tool and a prompt-type rule for their own design work. In each 10-minute task, participants generated concepts 'using the assigned image-generation system and specified prompt type', numbered them, and submitted one image they selected. No condition differs only in whose output is evaluated.

(c) Both tools are generative image generators, 'two distinct user-facing image-generation systems': Midjourney V6 (IGAS0) and ChatGPT-4o image generation (IGAS1), both accessed in March 2025. Midjourney ran at default resolution with random seeds and style about 750, ChatGPT-4o used a new chat window per task, and the researchers pre-configured all settings. ai_tool.name_model, role image_generation, and how_used match the text, including the post-hoc prompt compliance check.

(d) Arms A to D match the paper's four condition definitions. Every arm uses generative AI, and there is no no-AI or other-aid arm, so ai = generative_ai and comparison type ai_design (another AI configuration) are right. Caveat: the paper presents both tools as 'operational representatives of different alignment orientations' and names no default tool or prompt type. Which arm is labelled control is therefore the screeners' choice, which the form already lists in open_questions.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.3; p. 6, Sect. 3.2.3 and Fig. 1

confirmed.statement: Arms n_analyzed = 60 and n_randomized = null fit the text. The paper recruited 60 people, 10 per group, and Fig. 3 shows one submitted image per condition for every participant, listed by group. No count at allocation is printed.
preregistered = not_stated is right. The paper mentions no preregistration or registry.
The lab setting is stated: 'The experiment was conducted in a controlled laboratory setting.' Only the randomized part of lab_rct lacks support.

summary: The paper never says that anything was randomized: all 60 participants used generative AI in all four within-person conditions (Midjourney V6 or ChatGPT-4o image generation crossed with concrete or abstract prompts), the order came from a 4 × 4 balanced Latin square with no stated random allocation to its sequences, and the between-subjects groups were classified from a pre-test questionnaire (pp. 5-7). The form's randomized = not_stated, arms, ai_tool, and criterion 1 = unclear match the text, but design_class lab_rct claims a randomized experiment that the text does not support, so random assignment to generative-AI conditions is not established.
